At least, this is how the president’s press secretary, Sherzod Asadov, framed a new constitutional law that strengthens the administration’s status, grants lifetime immunity to its officials and extends its outreach. The Legislative Chamber passed the Law on the Administration of the President on August 6; the Senate approved it the very next day. There was no public discussion and the body of the law was not disclosed before the president signed it on August 14. The administration was launched to “provide information, analytical, organizational and supervisory support for the activities of the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan” in 2018, two years after Shavkat Mirziyoyev came to power. In 2018-2022 it was headed by Zaynilobiddin Nizomiddinov, and in 2022-2023 by Sardor Umurzakov. In that time, Mirziyoyev’s eldest daughter, Saida Mirziyoyeva, served as a deputy director of the Agency for Information and Mass Communications under the administration in 2019-2020, and as a deputy chairman of the Board of Trustees of the National Fund for Support and Development of Mass Media in 2020-2022. She started working as head of the Department for Communications and Information Policy of the Executive Office of the Presidential Administration in 2022 before becoming an assistant to the president in August 2023. At the same time, Umurzakov was moved to another position and the head-of-administration post was abolished. In June 2025 the post was re-established, and Mirziyoyeva was appointed as the head of the administration. The new law, which consists of four chapters and 34 articles, extends the first daughter’s power. The document establishes that the head of the administration is not elected, but appointed and dismissed by the president himself.

articles.title: India’s BrahMos at Sea: Implications for South Asian Stability
articles.excerpt: In May 2025, the confrontation between India and Pakistan was limited to the land and air domains. In the naval domain the two sides took to signaling and positioning but did not engage in active combat. At the start of the conflict, India deployed its naval aircraft carrier INS Vikrant for four days in the Arabian Sea but later moved it back to its base in Karnataka. The Pakistan Navy undertook counter-deployments with an operational offensive-defensive posture. It dispersed its surface combatants, intensified maritime ISR, and moved its coastal missile units into a state of heightened readiness. However, there was no confrontation between the two navies during the crisis. However, a few weeks after the announcement of the ceasefire between India and Pakistan, Indian Defense Minister Rajnath Singh visited INS Vikrant and issued a stern warning for Pakistan. He said, “If Pakistan tries anything nefarious again, the opening move might come from our Navy.” Since the May 2025 clashes, both states have actively invested in further strengthening the capabilities of their naval forces. Recently, the Indian Navy announced its plan to equip more frontline warships with BrahMos supersonic cruise missiles. The plan is to work toward a fleet-wide integration of the BrahMos weapon system by 2030. This development may also increase pressure on Pakistan to take both defensive and offensive measures to maintain naval parity in the region. Currently, the Indian Navy operates a diverse range of missiles for anti-ship and land-attack roles. This includes the BrahMos missile deployed across 20 major frontline combatant platforms, the Klub series deployed on Talwar-class frigates, Kh-35E Uran deployed on older systems, and French-made Exocet missiles and American Harpoon missiles on its diesel-electric submarines. However, the BrahMos system has proven its operational relevance for the Indian military after its combat use during the May 2025 crisis.

articles.title: ‘Latin Poison’: Kazakhstan’s Latinization in Russian Media Discourse
articles.excerpt: In July 2025, my feature titled “Scripts and Power: How Russian Media Frame the Latinization of the Kazakh Language” was published in The Diplomat. There, I argued, based on my analysis of over 200 articles, that Russian media views Latinization through a politicized lens and relies on conspiratorial, colonial, and nostalgic narratives in commenting on Kazakhstan’s script reform. Shortly after, Russian outlet Ritm Evrazii published a piece, “Latin Poison for Kazakhstan,” as a direct response to my feature. Its author, Vladislav Makarov, discussed “the bewilderment among Russians caused by Kazakh officials’ stubborn desire to ban the Cyrillic alphabet.” Makarov further argued that Moldovan or Azerbaijani cultures have not become known worldwide because of their switch to Latin and that the new alphabet serves to “tie [post-Soviet republics] to their new overlords.” This piece does not mean that my feature caused a significant stir in Moscow. Nevertheless, it is interesting evidence of how, in responding to an English-language feature about Kazakhstan’s script reform, Makarov reproduced the same Russia-centric narratives described in the original feature. In his words, Kazakhstan has been “connected to the Russian World for centuries,” thus justifying Russia’s commentary on Latinization. The script reform in Kazakhstan, aimed at transitioning the Kazakh language from Cyrillic to the Latin alphabet, has been ongoing since 2017. Among the official reasons for the script change are the intentions to strengthen Kazakh identity and language and to rectify the true Kazakh pronunciation, which was affected by the Soviet-imposed Cyrillic script. Conceived under Kazakhstan’s first president, Nursultan Nazarbayev, Latinization is to be fully implemented by 2031. Current President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev called for a cautious approach to Latinization.

articles.title: More and More Global Leaders Went to Chinese Colleges. Does That Matter?
articles.excerpt: On June 23, 2026, South Korean Prime Minister Kim Min-seok walked onto the campus of Tsinghua University in Beijing, where he had earned a law degree in 2010. “I believe that my time studying at Tsinghua University will remain one of the most beautiful memories of my life, forever cherished and held close to my heart,” he told his hosts. Kim had flown in from Seoul on early morning flights, he recalled, just to make it to class on time. (Kim has since resigned from office to become the chair of the ruling Democratic Party.) Three weeks earlier, Lao President Thongloun Sisoulith had stood in the dormitory room at the Central Party School where he had lived during a month-long program in 2000. “Though the campus has undergone some changes,” he said, “the places where I lived and studied remain just the same.” Both leaders returned to a Beijing alma mater within three weeks of each other. They are not alone. Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, the president of Kazakhstan, studied at the Beijing Linguistic Institute (now known as the Beijing Language and Culture University) in 1983-84 and speaks fluent Mandarin. In April 2026, Le Minh Hung took office as Vietnam’s prime minister; in 1996, he had completed a training course on market economy and financial analysis at Shanghai University of Finance and Economics. With four neighborhood countries now having top leaders who have studied in China, does this mark a new phase in Chinese educational diplomacy in its periphery, or is it little more than a biographical curiosity? Three forces explain the growing cohort of Asian leaders who spent time at Chinese schools. First, Chinese universities have risen sharply in global rankings. In the 2026 U.S. News Best Global Rankings, Tsinghua – a public institution that traces its roots back to 1911 – placed sixth globally, accompanied by 10 other mainland institutions in the top 100. A degree from a top institution in China now carries weight both at home and abroad.

articles.title: Takaichi Is No Abe: Japan’s New Conservative Politics
articles.excerpt: For many years, Japan’s current Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae has been portrayed by international media as the heir to Abe Shinzo’s political legacy. Her nationalist views, assertive security posture, and close ties to Japan’s conservative movement have made the comparison seem natural. There is good reason for the comparison. As Michael Green recently argued in Foreign Affairs, Takaichi has continued an important part of Abe’s strategic legacy: strengthening Japan’s defense capabilities, deepening the Japan-U.S. alliance, and responding more assertively to the challenge posed by China. From this perspective, Takaichi represents the continuation of a strategy that seeks to make Japan a stronger and more indispensable U.S. ally. But strategic continuity should not be confused with political continuity. After roughly 10 months in power, the differences between Takaichi and Abe are becoming increasingly difficult to ignore. Rather than simply reviving “Abe politics,” Takaichi appears to be developing a new political style of her own: more personalized, more confrontational, and more dependent on emotional mobilization through social media. If Abe represented a conservative politics tempered by strategic pragmatism, Takaichi may represent something closer to a new form of conservative populism. In other words, Takaichi may be Abe’s heir in grand strategy, but she is not necessarily adopting his tactics. The political methods emerging from Takaichi’s camp suggest a significant change in how Japan’s conservatives seek to mobilize domestic public support. The controversy over the use of artificial intelligence (AI) during the 2025 Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) leadership election and the 2026 House of Representatives election offers a revealing example.

articles.title: Can Discussions in Cambridge Help Afghans Build a Post-Taliban Future?
articles.excerpt: In the past, too many plans for Afghanistan have been designed far from the people expected to live under them. On the surface, the Cambridge Afghanistan Series, organized by the Mosaic Global Foundation, may seem to be more of the same. But the series is genuinely attempting something different, which is not to hand people of Afghanistan another foreign-made political formula, but to create a space in which Afghans themselves can identify the principles, institutions, and sequence required to reclaim their political future. On September 4 and 5, the Mosaic Global Foundation will convene the fifth Cambridge Afghanistan Series (CAS V) at Jesus College, Cambridge. It will bring together Afghan political voices, civil society actors, human rights advocates, academics, and other stakeholders to discuss pathways toward peace, inclusion, and prosperity. At CAS III in 2024, six major political factions, including two major armed resistance groups, presented their visions for Afghanistan. An independent examination found that, despite their public divisions, more than 90 percent of their proposals overlapped in substance. CAS IV in 2025 began a more open discussion of the remaining disagreements. I participated in CAS IV in 2025. I did not see complete unity, nor did I expect it. Afghanistan’s political actors carry different histories, represent different constituencies, bear different grievances, and have different ideas about the state. What I saw was something more modest but genuinely hopeful as major political currents, civil society, and human rights advocates from different ethnic backgrounds and communities gathered to discuss the future of their country and search for an Afghan-led solution. At a time when the Taliban has tried to erase political plurality inside Afghanistan, the sight of Afghans arguing across their differences, without denying one another a place in the conversation, offered a glimpse of another political culture.

articles.title: The Kuril Flashpoint: Putin’s Visit and the Future of Japan-Russia Ties
articles.excerpt: Russian President Vladimir Putin made his first visit to the Kuril Islands on August 12. He became the second Russian leader to visit the islands, after President Dmitry Medvedev’s landmark trip in 2010. More recently, Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin visited the islands in 2021. Putin’s recent visit prompted a protest from Japan, with Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae calling the visit an offense to the sentiments of the Japanese people and unacceptable. The islands have been the subject of an ongoing territorial dispute between Japan and Russia, both historically and under international law, for over 80 years. Russia calls the islands the Kuril Islands, and Japan calls them the Northern Territories; the volcanic islands lie at the heart of a territorial feud that has prevented the two countries from formally ending World War II, despite signing a joint declaration for restoring diplomatic relations in 1956. Putin’s recent visit has made it even harder to restore relations between the countries. There are 56 islands in the 1,300-kilometer (810-mile) archipelago that stretches from Russia’s Kamchatka Peninsula to Hokkaido, separating the Sea of Okhotsk from the Pacific Ocean. Japan claims four of the islands. These include Iturup (Etorofu in Japanese), Kunashir (Kunashiri), Shikotan, and Habomai, the southernmost islands and closest to Japan, just off the coast of Hokkaido. While Russia administers the islands as part of the Sakhalin region, Japan considers the four they claim as part of Hokkaido prefecture and argues that they are “illegally occupied” by Russia. In 1855, in the first treaty between tsarist Russia and Japan, the frontier between the two countries was drawn just north of the four islands closest to Japan. Twenty years later, a new treaty handed the entire chain to Japan, in exchange for Russia gaining full control of the island of Sakhalin.

articles.title: Principled Caution: Navigating AI in Asian Newsrooms
articles.excerpt: Across Asia, public interest media are turning to artificial intelligence (AI) to optimize under-resourced newsrooms. However, these outlets face a high-stakes reality: publishing AI-generated errors, factual inaccuracies, or “AI slop” risks undermining the public trust and credibility central to their legitimacy. At the same time, these media are also aware that they are operating in authoritarian contexts where AI-induced mistakes can lead to legal and political persecution. Hence, independent outlets in the Asia-Pacific – the media that produce journalism essential to democratic accountability – exercise “principled caution” when deploying AI. They exercise this caution not just because of a desire to maintain their reputation for accuracy. They also do so because there is a real risk of forced state closure, the freezing of assets, or the imprisonment of staff. This is the core finding of Asia Centre’s latest report, “Principled caution: How AI is used in public-interest media in Asia,” published in partnership with DW Akademie and supported by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development. Evaluating media ecosystems across eight Asian countries – Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Cambodia, Indonesia, Myanmar, Pakistan, and Uzbekistan – the study reveals how journalists are managing AI adoption. Rather than blind adoption, Asia’s independent public interest media are approaching AI through a careful and highly selective strategy. In structurally precarious environments where reporting errors can invite censorship, legal action, or operational shutdown, outlets consistently prioritize human editorial oversight over full-scale automation. The report identifies several key findings: First, AI usage in newsrooms remains assistive rather than transformative.

articles.title: What Does Japan Think of the Sudden Cut to South Korea-US Joint Drills?
articles.excerpt: On August 16, U.S. President Donald Trump scaled back military drills with South Korea. In a social media post, he cited three different explanations for the move: the cost of the exercises to the United States, his supposedly friendly relations with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, and his displeasure over perceived lack of South Korean support for the U.S. war effort against Iran. After Trump’s intervention, the annual Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise, which started on August 17, only ran through August 21 instead of the originally scheduled August 27. In practice, the first phase of the exercise – focused on defense – was preserved while the second phase – focused on counterattack – was canceled. In addition, live-training exercises were replaced with simulations. According to the South Korean new agency Yonhap, South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun told the legislature that “Neither our government nor U.S. officials knew what President Trump wrote on his Truth Social account.” In a meeting with the National Assembly Committee on Foreign Affairs and Unification, Cho said, “We were not notified in advance.” On August 24, the United States canceled the biennial Ssangyong drills, a large joint amphibious landing exercise, scheduled for September. This time, the justification was constraints on force availability caused by the Iran war. This announcement was not as abrupt, as the U.S. Marine Corps had officially notified Seoul back in June that its force availability would likely be constrained. On August 28, the United States, South Korea, and Japan announced that they will conduct the annual Freedom Edge drills, joint military drills to test readiness against North Korea’s missiles and nuclear weapons threat, from September 9 to 11. What is Japan’s perspective on the latest developments in the South Korea-U.S. alliance? Japan’s initial reaction has been muted.

articles.title: What a Chongqing Fandom Clash Reveals About China’s Gender Divide
articles.excerpt: Waving Chinese national flags and singing the military anthem are sights more commonly associated with state-sanctioned patriotic rallies. Yet on the night of August 18 along Chongqing’s Nanbin Road, young men used these patriotic symbols while marching against a seemingly bizarre enemy: teenage idol trainees of a boy-band talent agency and their female fans. What began as a localized dispute outside the headquarters of Shidai Fengjun (also known as “Time Fengjun,” or TF Entertainment), an agency that helped pioneer China’s idol-trainee industry, rapidly escalated into a prolonged public disturbance. For days, the area around the agency saw escalating street violence, culminating in a heavy police presence and roadblocks. The confrontation offered a glimpse into a broader dynamic in contemporary China: how online male grievances can spill into the streets, how nationalist symbols can be mobilized in gender conflicts, and how authorities struggle to contain the resulting unrest. The trouble began on August 15, when groups of male short-video livestreamers and “anti-fans” (黑粉) repeatedly gathered outside Time Fengjun’s office building. Many appeared to be seeking online traffic and attention. They burned and tore down fan posters, blocked company vans, and confronted the company’s young trainees, some reportedly as young as 11. They livestreamed the confrontations while shouting “jiahao” (嘉豪), a derogatory internet term mocking young men who try too hard to appear “cool.” The chant appeared intended as a deliberate provocation. The incident took on a broader gender dimension after a viral video clip circulated on August 17. The footage captured a female fan throwing a small object (variously reported as a power bank or water bottle) at a male provocateur, who responded by splashing water at her and appeared to move toward her aggressively.

articles.title: Militant Buildup in Areas Critical to China’s Economic Interests in Pakistan
articles.excerpt: With the China Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), a critical node of the Belt and Road Initiative in Pakistan, entering its second phase, insurgent and terrorist networks in Pakistan are strategically positioning themselves in areas critical to CPEC’s future. CPEC connects China’s western Xinjiang province with the Arabian Sea. It enters Pakistan from the northern Gilgit-Baltistan area and culminates at Gwadar Port in Balochistan province. While the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) is gradually increasing its footprint in Pakistan’s northern belt, the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) has ramped up attacks in Balochistan, multiplying China’s security challenges. The deteriorating security situation in southwestern Balochistan and northern Pakistan is expected to disrupt future CPEC projects and China-Pakistan economic cooperation, thereby weakening Pakistan’s economy. The timing of militant buildup in these areas is vital; it is happening against the backdrop of intense U.S.-China competition over critical minerals in Balochistan. Currently, China and Pakistan are discussing $1.8 billion in financing for the realignment of the Karakoram Highway’s (KKH) Thakot-Raikot section. In May 2028, when Diamer-Bhasha Dam becomes operational, a 280-kilometer section of KKH will be submerged in water. China has been delaying financing these projects for economic and security reasons. Concurrently, TTP has been increasing its presence in the area along the KKH. It is important to mention that in July 2021 and March 2024, two unclaimed suicide attacks targeting buses carrying Chinese nationals working on the Dasu Hydropower Project took place along the KKH. Though no terrorist group officially claimed these attacks, individuals and militant networks involved in these attacks had past affiliations with TTP.

articles.title: One Nation’s Dual Assault on Australia’s Structural Realities
articles.excerpt: Oceania | Politics | Oceania With a below replacement-level birth rate and a booming elder population, One Nation’s anti-immigration stance, combined with its critique of superannuation, is a toxic combo. A major structural issue facing most Western and East Asian countries at present is their below replacement-level birth rates. This has the potential to create an unfavorable dependency ratio – the problem of aging societies with a large cohort of retirees, but not enough workers to pay for pensions, healthcare, and other essential services. Yet simultaneously, many Western countries are experiencing an insurgence of populist, and often extremist, parties hostile to the one mechanism available to alleviate this problem: immigration. In Australia, this year has seen the rise of One Nation – previously a small fringe anti-immigrant party – now consistently polling in the mid-high 20 percent range. One Nation often matches the governing Labor Party’s poll numbers, and is polling far ahead of Australia’s other traditional major political force, the permanent coalition between the Liberal and National parties. One Nation’s reason for existence is to undermine Australia’s migration program – which it sees as a threat to their idea of the Australian nation. Yet as the party has ascended in the polls it has needed to branch out into other populist causes and conspiratorial theories to promote. One issue the party has landed on is Australia’s retirement savings scheme – known as superannuation. Australia’s superannuation scheme was made compulsory in its modern form by the Keating government in 1992, requiring employers to contribute a portion of workers’ wages into privately managed retirement funds. The contribution rate has gradually risen to 12 percent – paid on top of wages – and has created one of the world’s largest pools of retirement savings. It is accessible at 60 years old.

articles.title: Tokayev Sets Agenda for Kazakhstan as New Parliament Gets to Work
articles.excerpt: Kazakhstan’s new unicameral parliament, the Kurultai, gathered for its first session today. On August 23 the all-but-ordained Adilet party triumphed over an array of officially sanctioned opposition parties, winning a thumping 71 percent of the vote in the first election after Kazakhstan’s March constitutional revamp. According to the Central Electoral Commission, which registered new legislators in an official ceremony on August 27, Adilet will have 110 deputies of a possible 145 sitting in the new body, likely led by presidential advisor-turned-party leader Aibek Dadebay. As for its legislative agenda, all signs indicate that the Kurultai will largely pick up where the old parliament left off. Kazakhstan’s President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev spent the last week plotting a roadmap for the incoming Kurultai, and his to-do list is grounded in long-standing governmental priorities. On August 27, for example, citing the example of “several well-developed countries,” Tokayev said he planned to ask Kurultai deputies to consider banning social media for children under the age of 16, in what will essentially be a continuation of a bill submitted to parliament in June, according to local independent media outlet Vlast.kz. In a similar vein, speaking at an educators’ conference on August 26, Tokayev called on the government to take more urgent measures to implement his May presidential decree on the introduction of artificial intelligence into the national education system. The directive came as part of the country’s Year of Artificial Intelligence program, itself a continuation of the broader strategy on AI launched in 2025 following the creation of the Ministry of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development.

articles.title: Domestic Politics Is Making an India Visit Difficult for Bangladeshi PM Tarique Rahman
articles.excerpt: A visit to India by Bangladeshi Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is long overdue. Bangladeshi prime ministers have traditionally made India the destination of their first visit after coming to power. But over six months after Rahman’s inauguration, the much-anticipated visit is yet to happen. Meanwhile, the Bangladeshi PM has visited Malaysia and China. Delhi has invited Rahman to India for a bilateral visit as well as to participate in the upcoming BRICS summit that it is hosting in September. Rahman’s visit was initially seen in Bangladesh as a chance for Dhaka and New Delhi to reset relations that deteriorated after the ouster of the Sheikh Hasina government on August 5, 2024. However, the visit seems unlikely to happen. Indeed, it has brought Bangladesh’s domestic politics into the equation, with moves by the Rahman government to improve relations with New Delhi now risking criticism at home. Over the past several weeks, officials from both countries have been discussing a bilateral visit. According to a media report in mid-August that cited Bangladeshi diplomatic sources, the two sides were discussing dates for a possible visit. It was expected to happen between August 20 and 25. Preparations for the visit went pretty far. On August 21, the Indian President’s Office briefly issued a notice saying its Change of Guard ceremony would be cancelled because of a rehearsal for the ceremonial welcome of the Bangladeshi prime minister. However, the notice was withdrawn within an hour. It seems that Rahman’s visit will not happen. One of the main obstacles is Sheikh Hasina, who has been in India since she fled after her government was toppled. In November 2025, Bangladesh’s International Crimes Tribunal convicted her of crimes against humanity over the deadly crackdown on the 2024 uprising, and sentenced her to death in absentia. Dhaka has since formally asked India to extradite her so the verdict can be enforced.

articles.title: China’s Green Exports to Europe Are a Bright Spot Amid Trade Tensions
articles.excerpt: China’s economy showed further signs of stagnation in July, according to delayed figures released from China’s National Bureau of Statistics on August 17. But one economic bright spot China’s government could point to was sales of Chinese electric vehicles (EVs) to western Europeans. According to data gathered by Schmidt Automotive Research over the first five months of 2026, sales of Chinese EV models in western Europe rose to 14.2 percent of total EVs sold between January and May. This means around one in seven EVs sold in the region were Chinese-made, despite significant EU tariffs on Chinese EV exports since 2024. Such tariffs are not replicated in the United Kingdom, accounting for some, but not all, of the recent surge in Chinese EV sales in many western European markets. Despite growing trade tensions between the EU and China, the uptick in sales is being driven by consumer responses to two factors: conflict and climate change. Europe is having a record-breaking heatwave this summer. Soaring temperatures have brought drought, wildfires, and higher electricity bills for households and businesses as European demand for air conditioning rises. The rise in natural disasters and other fallout from climate change is causing mounting insurance costs and business losses across the continent. These changes are accelerating Europe’s move toward a greener economy as more households and firms buy heat pumps, solar panels and EVs to decarbonize their activities. Meanwhile, the on-again, off-again conflict between the United States and Iran since February has caused European petrol and diesel prices to surge. The fuel spikes have improved the attractiveness to European drivers of ditching fossil fuels and switching to a battery-powered vehicle less exposed to crude oil price swings. Many Chinese EV manufacturers were quick to respond to an increase in Western European demand for their products this year, incentivized by a severe price war in their domestic market.

articles.title: Transitional Justice or Political Retaliation? Bangladesh’s Journalists on Trial
articles.excerpt: An estimated 1,400 people died in the July uprising of 2024, which led to Sheikh Hasina’s ouster on August 5, 2024. To contribute to accountability, reconciliation, and a sense of justice for the Bangladeshi people, the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) was revived. Created in 2010 based on the 1973 ICT act, the tribunal was designed to prosecute atrocities committed during the 1971 Liberation War. It was heavily criticized – especially in 2011-2012 but throughout her tenure – for being used by Hasina to put opposition figures on trial for 1971-era crimes. The ICT was seen as politically instrumentalized and lacking due process. This year, three journalists and a secular writer were arrested and accused before the ICT of crimes against humanity through incitement in connection with their reporting. They have been imprisoned for almost two years now on a wave of murder charges in the regular courts. Human rights organizations have condemned the murder charges and have raised concerns that the tribunal may now be used against figures associated with the former governing order, including journalists. “The crimes committed against the student-led movement in July and August 2024, in which hundreds were killed, demand a proper accounting, and those responsible should face justice,” said Toby Cadman, a human rights lawyer and former advisor to the ICT’s Chief Prosecutor. “The victims and the country are entitled to a process directed at truth, justice and reconciliation rather than retribution, and that makes it all the more important that these trials meet the highest standards of due process – properly particularized charges, timely disclosure, effective access to counsel, and meaningful judicial review of detention.” Journalists Entangled in Legal Cases Four Bangladeshi journalists – Farzana Rupa, her husband Shakil Ahmed, Mozammel Babu, and Shyamal Dutta – and writer Shahriar Kabir have faced criminal proceedings connected to the uprising.

articles.title: China’s Tourism Industry Gains Momentum Thanks to Visa-Free Policies
articles.excerpt: In the first six months of 2026, China received 22.91 million visits from foreign nationals, up 20.4 percent year on year. The uptick is the result of China’s visa-free policy, which accounts for 77.7 percent of all foreign arrivals. Earlier this year, China announced that starting February 17, 2026 all ordinary passport holders from Canada and the United Kingdom can travel to its mainland for up to 30 days without a visa. The expansion in China’s unilateral visa-exemption program to include Canada and the U.K. followed recent visits to Beijing by leaders from the two countries as they seek to reset ties. According to China’s Foreign Ministry, the visa-free program – expected to run until December 31, 2026 – aims to foster people-to-people exchanges, the foundation for cross-cultural understanding, economic interdependence, and peaceful diplomatic relations. For the United Kingdom, which sees China as an important tourist destination as well as a source market, attempts to eliminate barriers to cross-border tourism are certainly a step in the right direction. Data from the U.K.’s Office for National Statistics showed that around 620,000 British people traveled to China in 2024. According to VisitBritain, the national tourism agency, in the same year, the U.K. welcomed 463,000 visitors from China (41 percent were holiday visits, in line with the market average), generating a total expenditure of 723.8 million pounds. In the coming years, a new report from VisitBritain estimates that China’s visitor market will be worth around £1.2 billion in terms of visitor spending in 2026. The agency forecast that tourism from China to the U.K. will expand rapidly, by 20 percent annually through 2030. Similarly, as Canada seeks to reset relations with Beijing, the newly implemented visa-free policy is expected to further facilitate two-way travel.

articles.title: SCO at 25: Institutionalizing Coexistence Without Convergence
articles.excerpt: When the leaders of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) gather in Bishkek on September 1, 2026, they will be celebrating a quarter-century journey: from an original six members in 2001 to now the world’s largest regional organization comprising 10 members – China, Russia, India, Pakistan, Iran, Belarus, and four Central Asian republics – with Afghanistan and Mongolia as observers, plus 15 dialogue partners stretching from from the South Caucasus to the Middle East, South, and Southeast Asia. But the 25th anniversary will also be an occasion for a reality check. At first glance, persistent intra-SCO tensions are clear: Russia has dragged Belarus into its war with Ukraine; Iran’s war with the United States has seen it attacking Bahrain, Qatar, Kuwait, the UAE, and Saudi Arabia; Afghanistan and Pakistan are engaged in a cross-border conflict; India and China have an unresolved border and occasional military tensions; India and Pakistan have a deeply adversarial relationship; and Cambodia just last year was embroiled in a border war with Thailand. All of these states are either members, observers, or dialogue partners in the SCO. Given that SCO specifically does not address bilateral problems, it has made no contribution to mitigating conflicts that, nevertheless, continue to complicate SCO deliberations. The question, therefore, is inevitable: what has the SCO achieved in the last 25 years? The answer may not be spectacular yet it remains critical for understanding Eurasia’s future trajectories. The SCO has institutionalized a unique experiment in building coexistence without convergences. The SCO’s expanded membership and agenda surely remain its most visible source of relevance. Its original purpose was comparatively narrow: confidence-building and border management among China, Russia, and the Central Asian states.

articles.title: AI, Scams, the Law, and Governance: A Conversation With David Tan
articles.excerpt: Governments across Southeast Asia are struggling with the arrival of artificial intelligence, both its endless possibilities that can improve everyday life and the threats posed by organized crime and the scam industries that have taken hold in the region. Singapore-based David Tan, co-director of the Centre for Technology, Robotics, Artificial Intelligence & the Law, says the predominant issues evolve around what he calls the three Ps: permanence, proliferation, and perniciousness. “We only need to regulate what’s truly important – what’s really pernicious, that proliferates, and has that permanent digital memory,” he said, adding: “Intimate sexual images, child abuse images, whether digital or not, that should be a priority.” Tan, who also heads Intellectual Property at the EW Barker Centre for Law & Business at the National University of Singapore, spoke with The Diplomat’s Luke Hunt about how to combat the negative impact and AI’s reach into financial markets, public health, and pop culture. Common law and legislation are key, as are online safety commissions. These commissions have been deployed by a core group of eight countries, Singapore and South Korea among them, where national authorities coordinate across borders through the Global Online Safety Regulators Network. But Tan said the industrialized scam industry is here to stay, with crime syndicates expected to grow and continue taking advantage of AI and in particular, deep fakes. “I think that one just has to be more vigilant as to the kind of fakes we get,” he said.

articles.title: The Tibet-Nepal Flood Is a Himalayan Climate Security Warning
articles.excerpt: The catastrophic flash flood that struck the Tibet-Nepal border on August 26 should not be treated simply as another Himalayan natural disaster. It is better understood as a warning from a rapidly destabilizing cryosphere, one that transcends political borders. The disaster exposed the growing collision between climate change, geological fragility, infrastructure expansion, and weak transboundary environmental governance. What happened along the Nepal-Tibet frontier reinforces an argument that climate researchers have increasingly made: the Himalayan-Tibetan ecosystem must be approached not merely as an environmental space but as a critical arena of transboundary climate and cryosphere security. Initial reports suggested that an earthquake had triggered the disaster. Subsequent analysis by the U.S. Geological Survey indicated something different: the seismic signal was generated by the collapse itself, rather than a preceding tectonic earthquake. A large section of a high-altitude glacier – located at roughly 5,200 meters in elevation – broke away and plunged approximately 1,200 meters toward the valley floor. The resulting ice-rock avalanche entrained enormous quantities of debris and appears to have temporarily obstructed the Lhende Khola River before releasing a devastating surge downstream. The tragedy was not simply a conventional flood produced by excessive rainfall. Nor does the evidence currently justify describing it as an earthquake-triggered disaster. It was a cascading high-mountain event in which ice, rock, gravity, water, and steep topography combined. The narrow Himalayan valleys then acted as conduits for an exceptionally fast-moving mixture of water, sediment, and boulders. The disaster therefore raises two questions that should extend well beyond its immediate aftermath. How safe is the accelerating infrastructure expansion across Tibet when the geological and cryospheric foundations of the plateau are becoming increasingly unstable?

articles.title: Nepal’s ‘Himalayan Tsunami’ Is a Warning for the Whole Region
articles.excerpt: For Nepali people, August 26 started like any other day, just another routine morning for the communities in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha, and Chitwan. But there is a saying in Nepal: “Disaster won’t come by making noise.” On Wednesday, people experienced that reality ruthlessly. By midday, that ordinary morning had turned into a nightmare. A sudden flood that crashed down from the northern side of the border devastated multiple districts of Nepal. The customs office of the Nepal-China border, Syaphrubeshi, Betrawati, Timure, and Trisuli area in Rasuwa district all suffered extensive damage. Entire villages were swept away. The floodwaters then rushed toward the Trishuli River, threatening more settlements in the areas of Nuwakot and Dhading. Over 30 bridges collapsed, 42 kilometers of roads were damaged or simply washed away, and communications were disrupted. Thousands of homes were swept away. More than 359 bodies have been recovered so far, and there are still thousands of locals missing. In addition, more than 644 tourists from 33 countries were reported missing. Security personnel themselves were reported missing. In China also, at least three people were killed and more than 500 people were reported missing. In both countries, rescue and recovery operations are ongoing. Bahrabise Bazar, Nepal, before and after the Aug. 26, 2026 flood. Photo via Wikimedia Commons. What exactly caused the disaster is still unclear, but experts believe a massive avalanche or landslide may have blocked the river, creating a temporary dam that eventually burst. It could have been a glacial lake outburst flood – if confirmed, that would be a warning for the entire Hindu Kush Himalayan region about the growing threat of climate crises. By 3:30 p.m. on Wednesday, the Bhotekoshi River had receded and returned to its original size. But that only made clear the devastation it had wreaked throughout the morning.

articles.title: Rahul Gandhi Ushers a New Style of Youth-Centric Politics in India
articles.excerpt: When Congress leader and Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi addressed women students at the Chhatron ki Goonj (Voice of Students) event in Pune last week, he urged them to “Smash the Patriarchy,” a message that resonated not just with his audience at the Pune event but with youth across the country. “India’s biggest strength, its asset,” Gandhi said, “is its 70 crore (700 million) women.” “Be loud, be proud. Fight for your space,” he told his young audience. Unsurprisingly, his speech raised the hackles of India’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). BJP leader and Union Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Kiren Rijiju questioned why Gandhi was “always target[ing] only Hindu? What about minority women…” Gandhi had not mentioned Hindus in his speech. However, the BJP, a Hindu nationalist party, chose to misquote the Congress leader in a bid to shift the discourse to a Hindu-Muslim communal one, a standard ploy of the BJP and other Hindutva organizations. Since the protests at New Delhi’s Jantar Mantar in June-July this year, India’s Gen Z has shown utter disdain for the BJP and its leaders and the kind of politics they engage in. Indeed, several protestors used expletives to mock BJP leaders. In a desperate attempt to win back their support, Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed Gen Z youth for the first time on the night of July 24 through an awkward hand-held Instagram reel, where he said he was “pained” and it was a “cultural shock” seeing “our young daughters” mouthing expletives against him and other BJP leaders. Modi’s speech was condescending. He spoke down to the protesters, viewing them through a patriarchal lens and addressing them as his daughters and sisters. He described them as “misguided” and said he had “forgiven” them. Modi’s speech infuriated Gen Z in general and women in particular, who have continued to target the BJP and its patriarchal mindset.

articles.title: Remembering a Genocide: The View From the Rohingya Camps
articles.excerpt: Every year on August 25, the Rohingya community around the world gather to commemorate Rohingya Genocide Remembrance Day. It is a day of mourning, expression, reflection, and hope. On this day, Rohingya people living abroad and in refugee camps hold banners, join together for mass prayers, recite poems, share their history, organize refugee exhibitions, and participate in social activities. All of these activities aim to remember their homeland and memories, and to honor their loved ones who were killed by the Myanmar authorities on August 25, 2017. For the Rohingya, August 25 is not just a black day. It is a day that has buried countless innocent Rohingya, that has mixed the tears of the Rohingya with blood, and that has forced more than a million Rohingya to flee to Bangladesh. On this day, the Myanmar military put into motion its plan to wipe out the Rohingya community from Myanmar’s Rakhine State under the pretext of responding to an attack on a police station. According to international human rights groups and Rohingya civil society organizations, more than 300 Rohingya villages were partially or completely destroyed following the Myanmar military’s attacks beginning on August 25, 2017. Rohingya women and girls were raped in front of their parents, husbands, and brothers. Children were thrown into fires, and people were burned to death inside their homes. Many were arrested and sent to jail; many family members still don’t know the whereabouts of their jailed family members. Property was looted, and mosques were destroyed. Many died after their trawlers were capsized or broken in the Naf River while fleeing to Bangladesh. Doctors Without Borders concluded that “[a]t least 9,000 members of the ethnic Rohingya minority died – most of them from violence – in Rakhine State, Myanmar” in the month after the violence began on August 25, 2017. “I witnessed the brutal massacre of my Rohingya community by the Myanmar military in 2017.

articles.title: Flash Flood Devastates China-Nepal Border Region
articles.excerpt: A devastating flash flood along the China-Nepal border has killed at least 160 people, with nearly a thousand more missing. The disaster centered on Nepal’s Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts, including the trading hub of Syabrubesi on the border. On the Chinese side, Gyirong County in Tibet was hit. Via Google Maps. Nepal’s Rasuwa District is marked in red. According to Nepali officials, the flood began at 8:40 a.m. on August 26, just three minutes after a magnitude 4.4 earthquake hit in Tibet, on China’s side of the border. That apparently caused a landslide involving both rock and ice from a Himalayan glacier. When the material flowed into the Lhende River in Tibet, known in Nepal as the Bhotekoshi, it caused the river to catastrophically overflow its banks. The Kathmandu Post summarized a Nepali-language explanation offered by Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA): The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said a preliminary study, based on an analysis of Planet Labs satellite imagery, indicates that a debris-laden flood entered the Lhende river after a glacial-rock slide occurred along the Nepal-China border, about 20 kilometres northeast of the Rasuwagadhi border point. The flood then flowed through Timure and entered the Trishuli river. What exactly transformed a relatively minor earthquake into a crushing flood remains unclear. The Kathmandu Post reported that both Nepal and China were struggling to get accurate information in the immediate aftermath of the disaster. Citing Nepal’s consul general in Lhasa, the capital of Tibet, the Post said that “neither Nepali nor Chinese authorities had been able to establish contact with security personnel deployed along parts of the Nepal-China border.

articles.title: AI Is Lowering the Barriers to China’s Information Warfare Against Japan
articles.excerpt: Japan’s Ministry of Defense recently released its 2026 Defense of Japan white paper, once again drawing attention to China’s rapid advances in artificial intelligence and their implications for the regional security environment. Yet the most immediate danger to Japan may not come from AI’s application to conventional military systems. Generative AI is also lowering the barriers for Chinese information operations targeting Japanese society. In late 2025, Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae made comments in the Diet linking a Taiwan contingency to Japan’s own security. Since then, disinformation targeting Japanese political figures and domestic issues has grown – not only in volume but also in sophistication. Research by organizations including the Sasakawa Peace Foundation and OpenAI suggests that China-linked influence operators are increasingly using AI to adapt their activities to Japan’s online environment and improve the efficiency of their operations. AI is beginning to erode what was once one of the most obvious weaknesses of Chinese information operations against Japan: the linguistic and cultural barrier. Content that once featured grammatical mistakes, awkward translations and unnatural expressions is becoming harder for ordinary users to identify at a glance. If these capabilities are deployed to interfere with elections, discredit politicians or amplify social divisions, their effects could extend far beyond any single piece of false information. A special report by Nikkei in February found that more than 400 China-linked social media accounts spread negative content about Takaichi during Japan’s House of Representatives election. Separately, the Yomiuri Shimbun, citing research by Japan Nexus Intelligence, reported that under a different set of criteria, thousands of coordinated accounts on X were involved in sharing and amplifying related content. The narratives did not focus solely on attacking Takaichi personally.

articles.title: How Taiwan Became Singapore’s Largest Trading Partner
articles.excerpt: In 2025, Taiwan overtook China as Singapore’s largest merchandise trading partner for the first time. According to Singapore’s Ministry of Trade and Industry, bilateral trade reached approximately S$170.3 billion (US$134 billion), ahead of Singapore’s trade with China (S$162.9 billion) and Malaysia (S$145.0 billion). One year earlier, Taiwan had ranked fourth. Singapore values Taiwan as a node in a diversified economic portfolio, but official diplomacy remains limited within the One China framework and Singapore has no incentive to revisit it. The AI Boom Much of the bilateral trade between Singapore and Taiwan involves the semiconductor industry. Both Taiwan and Singapore have heavily invested in their AI industries to take advantage of the global AI boom. Taiwan’s semiconductor industry accounts for over 60 percent of global foundry revenue and more than 90 percent of leading-edge chip manufacturing, while Singapore has built out its AI ecosystem to include public research, public service adoption, and diffusion into commerce and industry. In 2025, roughly 80 percent of Taiwan’s exports to Singapore were semiconductors and related products, while about 60 percent of Singapore’s exports to Taiwan consisted of semiconductor equipment and intermediate goods. The surge in trade runs both ways. Singapore’s non-oil domestic exports to Taiwan last year grew 37.4 percent – the strongest performance among its major trading partners. As both economies occupy different stages in the AI supply chain, they have formed a highly complementary and closely linked cooperative network in Asia’s AI industry chain. Taiwan fabricates the overwhelming share of the world’s leading-edge logic chips through TSMC and its foundry ecosystem. Meanwhile, Singapore supplies equipment, materials, assembly, advanced packaging, and test capacity, and operates as the regional logistics and headquarters hub through which chips and inputs circulate.

articles.title: Tarun Tejpal’s Conviction and India’s Discussions About the ‘Perfect Rape Victim’
articles.excerpt: She wore the wrong clothes. She was out at the wrong hours. She went to the wrong place. She is always in the wrong company. She was drunk. She invited it. There have been plenty of ways to dismiss a rape or sexual harassment survivor by simply blaming them. This is so commonplace that, in 2021, a district court in the western Indian state of Goa acquitted a prominent magazine editor, holding that the accuser did not look traumatized in the CCTV footage captured moments after the incident. Recently, a high court overturned the verdict, specifically dismissing the approach of scrutinizing how the survivor behaved. The high-profile case involves Tarun Tejpal, who was the editor of the investigative news magazine Tehelka. A female junior colleague accused him of rape in 2013. In the August 2026 judgement, the Bombay High Court sentenced Tejpal to 10 years’ imprisonment. The high court’s reliance on evidence rather than survivor behavior has been strongly welcomed by gender rights and civil rights activists and a section of journalists. “I believe the High Court judgment is important not just because of the individual involved, but because it reinforces a larger principle,” wrote political commentator Sujit Nair. Even in 2002, Indian laws allowed men accused of rape to show that the survivor was of generally immoral character.

Mamdani, 34 Jahre alt und selbst erklärter Sozialist, hat seit seinem Amtsantritt im Januar 2026 eine große Anhängerschaft in den sozialen Medien aufgebaut. Er setzt sich unter anderem für bezahlbares Wohnen in New York ein und erreichte im Juni, dass die Mieten von rund einer Million Wohnungen eingefroren werden.

articles.title: US-Militär fliegt erstmals seit Juli Angriffe in Iran
articles.excerpt: Die USA haben offenbar zwei iranische Raketenwerfer bombardiert – wohl, um eine erneute Verminung der Straße von Hormus zu verhindern. Iran spricht von Toten und Verletzten. 30.08.2026, 23.14 Uhr Ein Kampfflugzeug auf dem Flugzeugträger USS »Abraham Lincoln« Foto: AFP Das US-Militär hat nach Angaben übereinstimmender Medienberichte erstmals seit Ende Juli wieder Angriffe in Iran geflogen. Ziel seien zwei Raketenwerfer auf der iranischen Insel Larak gewesen, berichteten das Nachrichtenportal »Axios« sowie die Sender Fox News, CBS News und Al Jazeera. »Ich kann bestätigen, dass US-Streitkräfte heute früh zwei iranische ‌Abschussrampen auf der Insel Larak angegriffen haben«, sagte eine Person aus dem Umfeld der US-Regierung. Demnach sei der Angriff präventiv gewesen: Zuvor sei beobachtet worden, wie Einheiten der iranischen Revolutionswächter Vorbereitungen getroffen hätten, um Raketen mit Seeminen in die Straße von Hormus abzufeuern.Iranischen Staatsmedien zufolge wurden bei dem Angriff mehrere Soldaten und Zivilisten getötet und verletzt. Es werde nun eine »Reaktion und Bestrafung« aus Teheran geben. Zuletzt hatte US-Präsident Donald Trump verkündet, dass alle Seeminen in den internationalen Gewässern der Straße von Hormus geräumt worden seien. Iran habe man mitgeteilt, dass jedes Schiff, das neue Minen platziere, zerstört werden würde. Er verwies auf eine »Nulltoleranzpolitik« bei der Verminung der Meerenge, nachdem er bereits Mitte April ähnliche Drohungen ausgesprochen hatte. Krieg gegen Iran zunächst abgeflautTrump hatte die US-Angriffe auf Iran Ende Juli vorerst ausgesetzt – mit der Begründung, laufenden Verhandlungen über die Straße von Hormus und das iranische Atomprogramm eine weitere Chance zu geben. Zwei Tage später wurden neue Angriffe des US-Militärs in Iran gemeldet.

articles.title: Unglück vor Zypern: Kapitän der gesunkenen Fähre festgenommen
articles.excerpt: Jede »geringste Fahrlässigkeit« werde ans Licht kommen, verspricht Nordzyperns Ministerpräsident nach dem Kentern einer Fähre mit 267 Menschen an Bord. Der Kapitän und sieben Crewmitglieder sind festgenommen worden. 30.08.2026, 21.13 Uhr Ort des Unglücks: Die meisten Passagiere konnten gerettet werden, acht Menschen starben Foto: Ali Ruhluel / Anadolu Agency / IMAGO Nach dem Fährunglück mit mehreren Toten vor der Insel Zypern sind der Kapitän und sieben Crewmitglieder festgenommen worden. Das erklärte der Ministerpräsident der nur von der Türkei anerkannten Republik Nordzypern Ünal Üsal nach Angaben des nordzyprischen Staatssenders BRT. Die Verantwortlichen würden zur Rechenschaft gezogen, versprach er: »Ich sage das hier ganz klar. Jeder Aspekt dieses Vorfalls wird untersucht. Selbst die geringste Fahrlässigkeit wird ans Licht kommen«, sagte Üsal. Die Rettungsarbeiten gingen weiter. Die Zahl der Todesopfer stieg unterdessen auf acht, wie der türkisch-zyprische Verkehrsminister Erhan Arikli nach Angaben des Senders BRT sagte. Nach zahlreichen Menschen werde noch gesucht. Nach offiziellen nordzyprischen Angaben befanden sich insgesamt 267 Personen auf der Fähre, darunter 259 Passagiere und acht Besatzungsmitglieder. Die meisten konnten gerettet werden. Nach Behördenangaben war die Fähre – offenbar ein Katamaran – am Mittag kurz nach dem Auslaufen aus der Hafenstadt Kyrenia (türkisch: Girne) gekentert. Demnach drang Wasser in die Fähre ein, die Ursache dafür ist noch unklar. Die Fähre war auf dem Weg ins östliche Mittelmeer. Berichten zyprischer Medien zufolge drangen große Mengen Wasser über das Heck in das Schiff ein. Der Kapitän leitete demnach ein Notmanöver ein, um das Schiff zu wenden. Der Besatzung sei es jedoch nicht gelungen, den Wassereinbruch zu stoppen, woraufhin das Schiff an Stabilität verlor. Blick von Zypern auf die Unglücksstelle Foto: Yiannis Kourtoglou / REUTERS Der Notruf wurde türkischen Behörden zufolge vier Seemeilen vor der Küste abgesetzt.

articles.title: Nepal: Schulleiter rettete wohl Hunderte Schüler vor der Sturzflut
articles.excerpt: Die Entscheidung kam prompt: Ein Schulleiter in Nepal hat mit einer sofortigen Evakuierung wohl rund 900 Schülerinnen und Schülern das Leben gerettet. Zudem konnte er Schulbusse mit Hunderten weiteren Kindern auf dem Weg zur Schule rechtzeitig umdirigieren. »Ich erfuhr durch Anrufe von der Flutwelle – etwa 15 Minuten, bevor sie unsere Schule tatsächlich erreichte«, erzählte Rajenda Dawadi, Leiter der Sekundarschule in dem Ort Trishuli Baraar, der Nachrichtenagentur dpa. Zunächst hatten die BBC und die britische Zeitung »Daily Mail« von der Rettung berichtet. »Ich sagte mir: Wenn es keine Flut gibt, verlieren wir einen Schultag. Aber wenn es eine Flut gibt, verlieren wir alle unser Leben«, erzählte Dawadi.Die 900 Kinder in der Schule flüchteten demnach zu Fuß und einige mit einem Bus. Kurzzeitig sei Panik in der Schule ausgebrochen. Eine in Ohnmacht gefallene Schülerin wurde mit einem Moped in Sicherheit gebracht. »Hätten wir die Entscheidung zur Flucht zehn Minuten später getroffen, könnten wir alle – einschließlich der Schüler und mir – heute nicht mehr mit Ihnen sprechen«, zitierte die BBC den Schulleiter. Sekunden entscheiden über Leben und TodEine der geretteten Schülerinnen, die 16-jährige Yunisha, erzählte dem Sender, sie hätten sich nur Sekunden vor dem Hereinbrechen der Flutwelle in Sicherheit bringen können. Mit anderen sei sie einen schlammigen Weg hinter der Schule bergauf gerannt, als der Ort hinter ihr schon durch die Wasser- und Geröllmassen zerstört worden sei.Vom Schulgebäude blieb fast nichts übrig. Ein Lehrer und der Hausmeister, der noch schnell die Türen schließen wollte, kamen ums Leben.

articles.title: Trump hetzt Medienaufsicht auf TV-Journalistin Kristen Welker
articles.excerpt: US-Präsident Donald Trump bezeichnet negative Berichterstattung über ihn als »illegal«. Regelmäßig attackiert er Journalistinnen und Journalisten, die sich ihm gegenüber kritisch äußern. Nun hat es die TV-Moderatorin Kristen Welker getroffen. In einem Posting auf seiner Plattform »Truth Social« hat er ihr am Sonntag »absichtliche Ungenauigkeit« in ihrer Arbeit vorgeworfen. Er werde sie »für eine Rüge oder Bestrafung« bei der Medienaufsichtsbehörde FCC melden, schreibt Trump. Als Grund für seine Aufregung gibt der US-Präsident an, die Moderatorin der NBC-Sendung »Meet the Press« habe etwas behauptet, das nicht stimme. Es gehe um seine Unterstützung von Politikerinnen und Politikern, die bei den Zwischenwahlen zum Kongress antreten – in den USA ist die als »Endorsement« bekannte Empfehlung ein viel beachtetes Instrument in Wahlkämpfen. Welker behaupte, so Trump, er verzeichne dabei »gemischte Ergebnisse«. Mehr zum Thema 2 Min 14 Min 2 Min Für rechte Kandidaten in den USA gab es lange nichts Wichtigeres als eine Empfehlung von Donald Trump. Doch zuletzt fielen mehrere von ihm unterstützte Politiker bei Vorwahlen durch. Cory Mills etwa, seit 2023 Abgeordneter im Repräsentantenhaus und für seine Wiederwahl von Trump empfohlen, verlor kürzlich die parteiinterne Vorwahl für die Midterms. Auch anderen republikanischen Kandidaten, die »Trump-endorsed« waren, ging es so. (Lesen Sie hier mehr darüber. ) Als Gegenbeispiel bringt Trump den Erfolg von Darline Graham Nordone. Die Schwester des im Juli gestorbenen US-Senators Lindsey Graham tritt an dessen Stelle bei der Wahl im November als Kandidatin für die Republikaner an. Sie setzte sich in der parteiinternen Stichwahl im Bundesstaat South Carolina gegen Ralph Norman durch. Das sei die »größte Story« überhaupt, schreibt Trump, weil man ihren Sieg nicht erwartet habe.

articles.title: »ZDF Fernsehgarten«: Andrea Kiewel live von Biene gestochen
articles.excerpt: Die 61-Jährige beugte sich nach vorn und schüttelte an ihrem Ausschnitt. Die anderen Gäste versuchten zu helfen, so gut das in so einer Situation eben geht. (»Ich will jetzt nicht ganz reingucken«, schränkte einer der Helfer ein.)Dann rief die Moderatorin: »Das war eine Biene – oh nein, nein, nein – und die hat auch gestochen«, gefolgt von einem »Auauaua!«. Noch vorgebeugt, sagte Kiewel schnell den nächsten Musikact an – und schrie noch einmal auf. Gut zwei Minuten später war Kiewel wieder aus dem Off zu hören: »Oh Gott, so peinlich!«, sagte sie, »Zeigt mich nicht«, keiner wolle das sehen. Unterdessen hatte ihr aber offenbar jemand ein Kühlpad oder Ähnliches gereicht. Mit dem auf dem Dekolleté fand sie wieder zurück in die Spur – und moderierte die Livesendung noch gute eineinhalb Stunden weiter.

articles.title: Google zeigt seinen Nutzern jetzt, wo der »Lake America« liegt
articles.excerpt: Als Google einst antrat, der Welt zu zeigen, wie das so geht mit dem Internet, gab sich das Unternehmen ein informelles Motto: »Don’t be evil« – sei nicht böse oder tue nichts Böses.Offiziell war das nicht, stand aber im Vorwort des firmeninternen Verhaltenskodex – und dass dies nach außen getragen wurde, dürfte der Firmenspitze nicht unangenehm gewesen sein. Schließlich begründete es einen hehren Anspruch: ein aufrechtes, ethisch handelndes Unternehmen sein zu wollen. Weniger gierig als all die anderen, weniger skrupellos, weniger opportunistisch. Ein paar Hundert Milliarden Dollar später fiel wohl selbst den Gründern auf, dass das nicht mehr glaubwürdig war. Google hatte das Gros der direkten Konkurrenz in Grund und Boden gewalzt, den Internetwerbemarkt zu einem Oligopol weniger Techriesen gemacht und ganze Branchen destabilisiert. Als Google als Firma 2015 hinter dem kryptischen, bis heute allenfalls Aktionären präsenten Namen »Alphabet Inc.« verschwand, ging auch das schöne Motto verloren. Google agiert wie ein Fähnlein im Wind. Das mit dem »nichts Böses« stand im Verhaltenskodex nun noch in einem Nebensatz ganz am Ende – niemand konnte also behaupten, Google habe sich von der Ethik getrennt.Alphabet verpasste sich derweil ein neues, im Vorjahr des amerikanischen Trump-Falls geradezu hellsichtiges Motto: »Do the right thing«, also »Tue das Richtige«.Für wen und wozu? Das konnte jeder auffassen, wie er wollte. Seit diesem Sonntag kann man als US-Nutzer bei Google Maps auch den »Lake America« bewundern, wo man vorher den »Lake Ontario« fand. Seitdem agiert Google wie ein Fähnlein im Wind. Und der weht in den USA gerade aus der Richtung Donald Trumps. Nachdem der US-Präsident nach einem Streit mit Mexiko den Golf von Mexiko im vergangenen Jahr kurzerhand in »Golf von Amerika« umbenannte, heißt die Meeresbucht auch für Nutzer von Google Maps so – zumindest, wenn man aus den USA ins Internet geht.

articles.title: Hockey-WM: Deutschland schlägt Spanien im Finale und holt vierten WM-Titel
articles.excerpt: Die Spanier hatten Deutschland in der Zwischenrunde mit 2:1 die einzige Niederlage im Turnier zugefügt. Im Halbfinale setzte sich Spanien gegen Olympiasieger Niederlande durch. Deutschland hatte zuvor Argentinien mit 2:1 besiegt.Guter Start, dann kamen die SpanierDie Mannschaft startete zwei Tage nach dem Halbfinale gut in die Partie. Benedikt Schwarzhaupt (2. Minute) scheiterte nach einer frühen Strafecke zunächst an Spaniens Schlussmann Luis Calzado. Wenige Minuten später konnte Torjäger Justus Weigand (9.) das Zuspiel von Hannes Müller nach einem Konter nicht gefährlich auf das spanische Tor bringen. Nach dem Seitenwechsel kam das Team des Deutschen Hockey-Bundes (DHB) zunächst kaum gefährlich in die Hälfte des Weltranglistensechsten, der erstmals seit 1998 wieder im WM-Finale stand. Auf der Gegenseite verpasste Kapitän Marc Miralles (40.) Spaniens Führung nur knapp und setzte eine Strafecke haarscharf neben das deutsche Tor.Mit der ersten DHB-Gelegenheit der zweiten Hälfte sorgte Struthoff dann für großen Jubel in der Hockeyarena in Wavre. Nach einer Vorlage von Paul-Philipp Kaufmann umkurvte der Kölner den spanischen Torwart und schloss mit dem erlösenden Führungstreffer ab. Der Titelverteidiger zog sich mit der Führung im Rücken zum Ende der Partie immer weiter zurück, beschränkte sich aufs Verteidigen und brachte das 1:0 über die Zeit.

articles.title: Bundesliga: Werder Bremen verliert erst Jens Stage und dann in Freiburg
articles.excerpt: Dem SV Werder Bremen ist der Auftakt in die neue Bundesligasaison misslungen. Das Team von Trainer Daniel Thioune unterlag beim SC Freiburg 4:1 (2:0). Für den Europa-League-Finalisten der vergangenen Spielzeit trafen Yuito Suzuki (29., 48. und 55. Minute) und Igor Matanović (45.). Dariusz Stalmach erzielte den Treffer für Werder (76.) Vor dem letzten Spiel des ersten Spieltags steht Werder somit auf Tabellenplatz 16.Dabei mussten die Bremer bereits vor dem Spiel eine, wie Kapitän Marco Friedl sagte, »Hiobsbotschaft« verkraften. Mittelfeldspieler Jens Stage hat sich im Abschlusstraining am Samstag eine schwere Muskelverletzung im Oberschenkel zugezogen. Damit muss Werder mehrere Monate nicht nur auf seinen Führungsspieler, sondern auch besten Torschützen der vergangenen beiden Spielzeiten verzichten.Bremens Geschäftsführer Clemens Fritz sprach vor dem Spiel bei Dazn von einem »Riesenschock«, gab sich aber optimistisch, noch vor dem Ende des Transferfensters am Dienstag einen Ersatz für den Dänen verpflichten zu können. Statt Stage spielten in Freiburg zunächst die beiden Zugänge Ludovit Reis und Chuki im zentralen Mittelfeld. Im Angriff feierte Niclas Füllkrug sein Comeback in der Bundesliga nach seiner missglückten Zeit bei West Ham United und der AC Mailand .Für Torgefahr sorgten zunächst aber weder Füllkrug noch andere Spieler auf dem Feld. Beide Teams agierten zunächst zögerlich, erst nach 20 Minuten erhöhten die Freiburger die Schlagzahl, ohne wirklich gefährlich zu werden. Erst mit einer Ecke von Niklas Beste, die Yuito Suzuki einnickte, kam Freiburg zur Führung. Im Anschluss verpasste Beste den nächsten Treffer mit einem Distanzschuss (41.), der knapp über das Tor flog. Besser machte es wenig später Matanović aus 20 Metern. Sein Schuss ins linke Eck markierte den 2:0-Halbzeitstand.

articles.title: Esther Schweins macht Ausbildung zur Trainerin für Stuhl- und Rollatortanz
articles.excerpt: Schauspielerin Schweins: »Tanzen verbindet Bewegung, Gleichgewicht, Koordination, Gedächtnistraining, Musik und soziale Begegnung« Foto: Willy C. Randerath / Future Image / IMAGO Esther Schweins war Kandidatin in der diesjährigen Staffel der RTL-Show »Let’s Dance« und musste diese wegen gebrochener Rippen vorzeitig verlassen. Doch mit dem Tanzen ist noch lange nicht Schluss, Schweins hat große Freude daran gefunden. Die 56-jährige Schauspielerin absolviert nun sogar in Mainz eine Ausbildung zur Fachtanzlehrerin für Senioren. »Ich habe meine Mutter im letzten Jahr in eine Pflegeeinrichtung der Caritas bringen müssen und dort zum ersten Mal Stuhltanz gesehen«, sagte Schweins. Inzwischen kennt sie sich mit Stuhl- und Rollatortanz aus, ebenso mit Tanzgruppen für an Parkinson oder Demenz erkrankte Menschen.Wegen des positiven Einflusses von Tanzen auf die Gesundheit und der präventiven Wirkung auf Alterungsprozesse setzt sich Schweins für »Tanzen auf Rezept« ein. »Die Idee ist überhaupt nicht so wild. In Großbritannien gibt es das schon.« »Tanzen verbindet Bewegung, Gleichgewicht, Koordination, Gedächtnistraining, Musik und soziale Begegnung«, erläutert Schweins. »Es fördert die kognitive Leistungsfähigkeit, senkt das Sturzrisiko, stärkt Herz und Kreislauf und natürlich auch die Lebensfreude.« Und: »Es wirkt auch gegen ein weiteres großes Gesundheitsrisiko unserer Zeit, die Einsamkeit.« So ein wissenschaftsbasiertes Präventionsangebot sei angesichts des bevorstehenden tiefgreifenden demografischen Wandels absolut sinnvoll, betonte Schweins. Der Anteil der Senioren werde weiter wachsen und das Gesundheits- und das Pflegesystem stießen jetzt schon an ihre Grenzen. Mehr zum Thema 4 Min 10 Min TV-Tango für Mutter LieselotteDer Allgemeine Deutsche Tanzlehrerverband (ADTV) habe bereits rund 400 Fachtanzlehrer für Senioren bundesweit ausgebildet. Dazu kämen noch die Programme anderer Tanzclubverbände. Schweins trat selbst im Frühjahr in der 19.

articles.title: Costa Rica: Deutscher Konsul Mario Genz bei Unfall in Lagune tödlich verunglückt
articles.excerpt: In Costa Rica ist der deutsche Konsul Mario Genz bei einem Unfall in einem Freizeitzentrum ums Leben gekommen. »Mit großer Trauer müssen wir die tragischen Meldungen über den Tod unseres Kollegen in Costa Rica bestätigen«, verlautete am Sonntag aus dem Auswärtigen Amt in Berlin. »Unsere Gedanken sind bei seiner Familie und bei allen, die ihm nahestanden.« Das Auswärtige Amt bestätigte dem SPIEGEL den Tod des Diplomaten. Zuvor hatte bereits das Außenministerium des zentralamerikanischen Landes im Onlinedienst X die Nachricht bestätigt und den Angehörigen sein Beileid ausgesprochen.Geübter Taucher und SchwimmerDer 53-Jährige war rund 75 Kilometer nördlich der Hauptstadt San José in einem Freizeitzentrum am Ufer der Lagune Río Cuarto verunglückt, wie die Leitung des Erholungsortes mitteilte. Der deutsche Diplomat sei beim Schwimmen in der Lagune aus zunächst ungeklärter Ursache in Not geraten. Costa-ricanische Medien hatten zuvor berichtet, Genz sei ertrunken, nachdem sein Kajak gekentert sei.

articles.title: Ruder-WM in Amsterdam: Oliver Zeidler feiert seinen vierten Titel im Einer
articles.excerpt: Einer-Dominator Oliver Zeidler hat sich seinen Titel bei der Ruder-WM zurückgeholt und sich zum vierten Mal zum Weltmeister gekrönt. Im Finale auf der Bosbaan in Amsterdam setzte sich der deutsche Olympiasieger von 2024 in 6:35,22 Minuten überlegen gegen den Belarussen Jauhen Salaty (6:38,33) und den Norweger Jonas Slettemark Juel (6:44,03) durch. »Ich hatte einen sehr guten Rhythmus – und konnte am Ende noch einen Sprint ziehen«, sagte Zeidler im Siegerinterview, ehe er seiner Freundin Sofia in die Arme fiel: »Meine ganze Familie ist hier und kann mit mir feiern.«Keine Niederlage in diesem JahrZeidler beendet die Saison damit ungeschlagen. Anfang August war der 30-Jährige im italienischen Varese in Rekordzeit zu seinem vierten EM-Titel gestürmt, in Amsterdam dominierte er sämtliche Läufe auf dem Weg ins Finale am Sonntag nach Belieben. Schon nach 500 Metern lag er deutlich vor der Konkurrenz. Die angepeilte Weltbestzeit des Neuseeländers Robert Manson (6:30,74) verpasste er. Im vergangenen Jahr hatte sich Zeidler auf sein Studium in Lausanne konzentriert und trotz stark reduzierten Trainings bei der WM in Shanghai den zweiten Platz hinter Stefanos Ntouskos belegt. Der Grieche war diesmal im A-Finale nicht dabei, belegte insgesamt nur den zehnten Platz.

articles.title: Im Test: Wechselwillige Gepäckträgertaschen
articles.excerpt: InLock heißt ein neues Taschensystem des schwedischen Träger- und Taschenspezialisten Thule. Das Versprechen: Diese Fahrradtaschen haben keine festen Haken, können aber schnell und sicher in den Gepäckträger eingehängt werden – sofern dieser entsprechend ausgerüstet ist. Wofür braucht man das? Immer dann, wenn die Tasche nicht ausschließlich für den Transport am Gepäckträger eingesetzt werden soll. Sondern auch auf Fußwegen, in Bus und Bahn und beim Einkaufen. Oder wenn man mit ihr auch im Büro oder an der Uni eine gute Figur machen will.Wie gut sich InLock in der Praxis schlägt, haben wir mit zwei Taschen von Thule ausprobiert. Und sie mit dem Quick-Lock3.1-Trägersystem von Ortlieb verglichen. Hier ist der Ansatz vergleichbar: Auf die beim Umhängen und Tragen störenden Haken wird auch bei Ortlieb verzichtet. Es gibt lediglich flache Halter an der Tasche – und Gegenstücke am Gepäckträger. Welches System besser ist, klärt dieser Test. Das neue InLock-System von Thule hat den großen Vorteil, dass die Taschen keine Hartplastik-Elemente für eine Halterung benötigen und daher auch auf der Rückseite weich und optisch unauffällig sind. Allerdings ist das Einhängen etwas umständlich und der Gepäckträger muss mit einem großen Adapter nachgerüstet werden. Bei Ortliebs Quick-Lock3.1 haben die Taschen drei flache Halter auf ihrer Rückseite. Wer sich daran nicht stört, wird bei Ortlieb mit einem breit gefächerten Taschenangebot und dem sehr einfachen Ein- und Aushängen der Taschen belohnt. Sollte irgendwann eine Aufnahme an den Taschen defekt sein, kann sie bei QL3.1 ausgetauscht werden.Die Einzeltests lesen sie unten.InLock von ThuleQuickLock 3.1 von Orlieb Foto: Markus Linden / DER SPIEGEL Bei Thule muss vor dem Einsatz der Taschen geschraubt werden. Und zwar eine Adapterplatte an den Gepäckträger. Denn ohne den Adapter mit seinem breiten Bügel können die Taschen nicht eingehängt werden. Die Platte wird an drei Punkten an einer Seite des Gepäckträgers befestigt.

articles.title: Waldbrände verhindern: Wie ein Förster Bäume für die Zukunft wappnet
articles.excerpt: Die Fichten stechen aus dem Grün hervor. Ihre hochgewachsenen Kronen überragen alles andere: Buchen, Douglasien, Eichen und Jan Meyer-Hamme, der zwischen den Bäumen auf dem Waldboden hockt. Auf seinen Schuhen krabbeln Ameisen herum. Den 39-Jährigen stört das nicht. Er sieht sich gerade einen Ahorn-Sprössling an. »Der wurde stark verbissen«, urteilt Jan. Das heißt, Wildtiere haben die Knospen des Jungbaums abgekaut. »Der hat keine Chance mehr, groß zu werden.« Jan ist Förster. Seine Arbeitsplätze sind der Wald und ein Büro in Neumünster. Dort befindet sich die Zentrale der Schleswig-Holsteinischen Landesforsten, bei denen Jan angestellt ist. Der Betrieb ist für alle Wälder verantwortlich, die dem Land Schleswig-Holstein gehören. Zu­sammengerechnet ist die Fläche ungefähr so groß wie rund 75.000 Fußballfelder.Ein Förster allein reicht für so viel Holz nicht aus. Insgesamt sind den Waldflächen 31 Revierleiterinnen und Revierleiter zugeteilt. Sie kümmern sich unter anderem um den Baum­bestand, halten die Augen nach Schädlingen offen oder planen die Holz­ernte. »Solche Aufgaben haben die meisten Leute im Kopf, wenn sie an Försterinnen und Förster denken«, sagt Jan. Was ist das Schönste an dem Beruf?»Nachhaltig zu arbeiten. Es ist unsere Aufgabe, den Wald für die nächsten Generationen zu erhalten. Das ist ein tolles Gefühl.«Und was ist das Schlimmste?»Mitzubekommen, dass viele Leute keinen Respekt mehr vor der Natur haben. Manche benehmen sich wie die Axt im Walde und lassen zum Beispiel ihren Müll zurück.«Wie viele Försterinnen und Förster gibt es in Deutschland?Eine genaue Zahl dazu gibt es nicht. In Deutschland sind rund 35.000 Menschen im Bereich der Forstwirtschaft beschäftigt. Davon arbeitet aber nur ein kleiner Teil als Försterinnen und Förster.Wie lange dauert die Ausbildung?Normalerweise sechs bis acht Semester, also drei bis vier Jahre. So lange dauert es, Forstwirtschaft oder Forstwissenschaft zu studieren.

articles.title: Unglück vor Zypern: Fähre kentert mit 267 Menschen an Bord
articles.excerpt: Gerettete Passagiere in Nordzypern: Ursache des Unglücks ist noch unklar Foto: REUTERS Vor der Küste Zyperns ist eine Fähre mit 259 Passagieren und acht Besatzungsmitgliedern gesunken. Mindestens sieben Menschen seien gestorben, sagte der nordzyprische Präsident Tufan Erhürman dem Sender CNN Türk. Die Einsatzkräfte suchten noch nach 23 Vermissten. Die Fähre – offenbar ein Katamaran – hatte den nordzyprischen Hafen Kyrenia um 12.30 Uhr Ortszeit verlassen und war auf dem Weg zum türkischen Hafen Tasucu im östlichen Mittelmeer. Das Schiff kenterte kurz nach dem Auslaufen. Die Ursache ist noch unklar. Empfohlener externer Inhalt An dieser Stelle finden Sie einen externen Inhalt von YouTube, der den Artikel ergänzt und von der Redaktion empfohlen wird. Sie können Ihre Zustimmung jederzeit wieder zurücknehmen. Externen Inhalt anzeigen Ich bin damit einverstanden, dass mir externe Inhalte angezeigt werden. Damit können personenbezogene Daten an Drittplattformen übermittelt werden. Mehr dazu in unserer Datenschutzerklärung. Berichten zyprischer Medien zufolge drangen große Mengen Wasser über das Heck in das Schiff ein. Der Kapitän leitete demnach ein Notmanöver ein, um das Schiff zu wenden. Der Besatzung sei es jedoch nicht gelungen, den Wassereinbruch zu stoppen, woraufhin das Schiff an Stabilität verlor. Der Notruf wurde türkischen Behörden zufolge vier Seemeilen vor der Küste abgesetzt. Ein Augenzeuge berichtete türkischen Medien, dass Passagiere die Crew zunächst vergeblich gewarnt hätten, dass Wasser ins Schiff laufe. Erst spät sei der Besatzung demnach der Ernst der Lage bewusst geworden. Die Passagiere seien dann ins Meer gesprungen, »wer eine Schwimmweste fand, sprang damit hinein; wer keine fand, sprang einfach ohne ins Wasser«. Er glaube, dass einige Menschen im Inneren der Fähre sich nicht hätten befreien können.

articles.title: Eurowings-Maschine muss wegen Dampfes außerplanmäßig landen
articles.excerpt: Eigentlich sollte Flug EW590 am Samstagabend um 21.45 Uhr in Palma de Mallorca ankommen. Doch statt auf der Baleareninsel landeten die Passagiere, die in Köln an Bord gegangen waren, gegen 22 Uhr in Paris. Dort hatte die Boeing 737 wegen Dampfentwicklung aus einer Bordküche außerplanmäßig landen müssen, wie ein Sprecher der Fluggesellschaft Eurowings sagte.Laut einem Bericht auf tagesschau.de war die Quelle ein Ofen in der Küche. In acht Kilometer Höhe habe das Flugzeug ein Notsignal gesendet. Da es sich zu dem Zeitpunkt knapp südlich der französischen Hauptstadt befand, entschieden sich die Piloten demnach für eine Landung am Pariser Flughafen Charles de Gaulle.Die 131 Passagiere hätten Hotelübernachtungen und die nötigen Transfers angeboten bekommen und würden auf die nächstmöglichen Flüge umgebucht, sagte der Sprecher. Die außerplanmäßige Landung sei vorsorglich und unter dem Flugprioritätenstatus »normal« erfolgt. »Die Sicherheit der Passagiere und der Crew war zu keiner Zeit gefährdet«, betonte Eurowings. Verletzt worden sei niemand. Den Flug hatte die tschechische Airline Smartwings im Auftrag der Lufthansa-Tochter Eurowings durchgeführt. Beruflich ist er viel unterwegs, doch seine extreme Flugangst bremste den Filmproduzenten Benedikt Böllhoff aus. Hier erzählt er, wie er sich von der Panik vor dem Fliegen befreien konnte.
